title: Accelerating LLM Serving for Multi-turn Dialogues with Efficient Resource Management
problem: Current LLM serving frameworks recompute attention keys and values for all prior turns on each new query in a multi-turn dialogue, incurring substantial redundant compute overhead. Additionally, the long accumulated prompt lengths from multi-turn context cause head-of-line blocking under FCFS scheduling, underutilizing GPU resources.
motivation: Multi-turn chat interactions are the dominant LLM serving pattern, but serving frameworks optimized for single-request throughput suffer disproportionate latency and GPU underutilization as conversation length grows.
method: The paper introduces efficient resource management for multi-turn LLM serving by preserving KV-cache state across turns to eliminate recomputation of prior-turn attention keys and values. A new scheduling policy replaces FCFS with a length-aware or priority-based scheduler that avoids head-of-line blocking by reordering or preempting long-prompt requests. KV-cache memory is managed dynamically to balance cache retention across concurrent multi-turn sessions, trading off memory capacity against recompute cost.
key_novelty: Cross-turn KV-cache retention combined with a head-of-line blocking-aware scheduler specifically designed for the multi-turn dialogue serving regime.
contributions: Characterization of multi-turn dialogue as a distinct LLM serving workload with unique KV-cache and scheduling challenges.
Cross-turn KV-cache management to eliminate redundant attention recomputation across dialogue turns.
Scheduling policy that mitigates head-of-line blocking for long accumulated prompts in multi-turn settings.
GPU resource utilization improvements demonstrated on multi-turn chat benchmarks.

metrics.other: GPU utilization improvement and latency reduction for multi-turn dialogues (details in full paper)

limitations: KV-cache retention across turns increases memory pressure; the tradeoff with batch size and concurrent session count is not quantified in the abstract.
primary_theme: multi-turn KV-cache management and scheduling for LLM serving
